title: What shape do the creases of a folded sheet make?
description: A sheet is folded into a quarter and one slanting crease is made across the corner. The folds are the diagonals of the opened shape, and they bisect each other at right angles, which makes a rhombus. Keeko doubts that the creases always make a square.
teaching_notes: One idea: the folds of a quarter-folded sheet become diagonals that bisect each other at right angles, so the creases make a rhombus, and equal cuts on both folds make it a square. Watch for students who think neat folds always give a square.

source: Which Quad? Gameplay: fold a sheet into a quarter, make a triangular crease at the corner in the middle of the paper, open the sheet, and fold again to get a square.
video_script.why: The child sees that the two folds become diagonals that bisect each other at right angles, so the creases make a rhombus, and that equal cuts on both folds give a square.
video_script.substitution: the book's own sheet folded in half and then into a quarter, with one slanting crease across the corner at the middle of the sheet
video_script.anchor: a paper sheet folded into a quarter with one slanting crease across the corner at the middle
video_script.wrong_answer: the creases always make a square
video_script.wrong_move: Keeko thinks the creases always make a square because quarter folds are neat, but the crease can cut unequal lengths along the two folds.
video_script.payoff_line: The creases make a rhombus, and equal cuts on both folds give a square

final_answer.value: A rhombus; fold the crease at 45°, cutting equal lengths on both folds, to get a square
final_answer.spoken: the creases make a rhombus, and equal cuts on both folds give a square

hold_back: A rhombus; fold the crease at 45°, cutting equal lengths on both folds, to get a square
never_show: the creases named a square without equal cuts
maths_rules: the two folds cross at right angles at the centre O of the sheet
each fold is a mirror line, so unfolding gives OR = OP and OS = OQ
the folds PR and QS are the diagonals of PQRS, and they bisect each other at O at right angles
the four triangles at O match, so PQ = QR = RS = SP and PQRS is a rhombus
equal cuts OP = OQ make the diagonals equal, so the rhombus is a square
triangle POQ is right angled with OP = OQ, so the crease makes 45 degrees with each fold
video_script.design: One idea: the folds become the diagonals of the opened shape. One folded sheet stays on the board, then opens, and each fact is marked on it in turn.

narration: <bookmark mark='doubt'/>Keeko thinks the creases always make a square, because quarter folds are neat.
<bookmark mark='long'/>But the crease can run far along one fold and only a little along the other.
<bookmark mark='fix'/>Then the diagonals are unequal, and the shape is a long thin rhombus, not a square.
